classification.difficultyReason: Read the vertex, calculate intercepts by setting each coordinate to zero, and combine these features into a sketch. Interpret square equations to distinguish two crossings, tangency and no real intercepts.

content.prompt: Sketch the following parabolas, labelling the turning point and any intercepts.

answer.worked:
The turning point is $(-1,4)$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0+1)^2+4\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)^2+4&=0\\(x+1)^2&=-4\end{align*}$$
A real square cannot be negative, so there are no $x$-intercepts. Sketch an upward-opening parabola with axis $x=-1$.

spec.description: Complete ungridded solution sketch with turning point and y-intercept labelled; no x-intercepts.

answer.worked:
The turning point is $(0,-5)$.

At $x=0$, $y=0^2-5=-5$.

At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-5&=0\\x^2&=5\\x&=\pm\sqrt5\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola symmetric about the $y$-axis through the labelled intercepts.

answer.worked:
The turning point is $\left(\frac32,-\frac{25}{4}\right)$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\left(-\frac32\right)^2-\frac{25}{4}\\y&=\frac94-\frac{25}{4}\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}\left(x-\frac32\right)^2-\frac{25}{4}&=0\\\left(x-\frac32\right)^2&=\frac{25}{4}\\x-\frac32&=\pm\frac52\\x&=-1\text{ or }4\end{align*}$$
Sketch an upward-opening parabola with axis $x=\frac32$ through these intercepts.

$$\begin{align*}y&=\left(\frac73\right)^2-\frac{16}{9}\\y&=\frac{49}{9}-\frac{16}{9}\\y&=\frac{11}{3}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\left(x+\frac73\right)^2-\frac{16}{9}&=0\\\left(x+\frac73\right)^2&=\frac{16}{9}\\x+\frac73&=\pm\frac43\\x&=-\frac{11}{3}\text{ or }-1\end{align*}$$
